translation_notes: prefixes: rdf: <...rdf-syntax-ns#>, rml: <http://w3id.org/rml/> (all RML_* constants of morph_kgc.constants share this one namespace, so every rdflib.term.URIRef(RML_X) becomes rml:x).

The region is a bare top-level for-loop statement, not a function: it reads free names yarrrml_mapping, mapping_graph, tm_id_to_norm_tm_ids and the RML_* constants and helper functions (_add_source, _add_template, _translate_yarrrml_function_to_rml) that live elsewhere in yarrrml.py/constants.py. Added shim.py with the constants and verbatim helper functions plus a make_fixture() covering every branch (reference/template/constant subjects, quoted and quotedNonAsserted triples maps, a function-valued subject and predicate, a join condition, an explicit termType, a referencing object map, and the implicit-blank-node subject when 'subjects' is absent).

mapping_graph is reassigned by the helper functions (_add_source, _add_template, _translate_yarrrml_function_to_rml) which mutate and return the SAME graph object; each such reassignment is followed by a fresh `@graph mapping_graph` per corpus/0xx's rule that @graph captures the value at its line, not the name.
The helper functions themselves keep .add() (they are shim context, out of scope for this region's translation, called identically from both original.py and translated.ldpy).

run_pair's entry/fixture modes assume a function or full-module comparison; this region is a script fragment referencing free globals, so driver.py seeds them directly and compares the resulting mapping_graph by isomorphism instead of using run_pair.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the PO term map `mapping_value['predicateobjects'][position]` and the subject map get local names; a str term map is normalised to {'value': str}, which removes the two str branches (the dict path then does the same template call and finds no condition/type keys); the subjectMap triple is hoisted out of the subjects/no-subjects alternative; the duplicated quoted/quotedNonAsserted loops and the duplicated join-condition block become two module-level helpers `_add_quoted` and `_add_join_condition` called at both sites (the condition dict is passed whole so that a missing 'parameters' still raises after the joinCondition triple); the two term-type if/elif chains become a `term_types` dict guarded by a tuple membership test (a tuple, not the dict, so an unhashable type value still raises ValueError and not TypeError); in the PO dict branch the referencing-object-map case is tested first (`'mappings' in term_map and 'function' not in term_map`) so the three other cases share one property triple, the ref_tm lookup still running before any triple of that branch is written; `rdflib.term.URIRef/Literal` become `rdflib.URIRef/Literal`; consecutive adds become `mapping_graph += [...]`.

The reassignments `mapping_graph = _add_...(mapping_graph, ...)` are kept on both sides (the helpers' contract returns the graph); optimized.ldpy therefore keeps a `@graph mapping_graph` after each one, as the translation does.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `+{ }` everywhere, the two triples of the no-subject case and of the referencing object map each in one island, `rml:constant []` for the fresh blank node, `a` for rdf:type, `f<{ref_tm}>`, `f<{mapping_id}>` and `f<{term_map['datatype']}>` for the URIRef calls (no @base in scope), term_types holding prefixed names; the join-condition literals are bare interpolations (a str slice), but `rdflib.Literal(term_map['language'])` is kept because a YAML null would give Literal('None') in the original where a bare interpolation raises.
No exception to the symmetry: every restructuring is in both files.
The anonymous blank node `[]` used in `+{ }` has no label in the closed construction vocabulary; it is not listed in optimized_constructions.
